speaker: alice
text: Scientists have created what I'm calling 'magic magnetic algae' that literally pulls microplastics out of water. These clever little organisms produce orange-scented oil that binds to those tiny plastic bits floating around in our waterways.

speaker: charlie
text: Like a microscopic cleanup crew with a citrus twist. But the real game-changer comes from underground - researchers have discovered that certain fungi naturally store carbon dioxide in soil for decades.

speaker: alice
text: These fungal networks are already working beneath our feet, locking away more carbon than we thought possible. Instead of fighting nature, we're finally learning to work with it. That's the kind of partnership that gives me hope.
